comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C2, C27, C33-C37 regarding pY peptides as primary regulators of PI3Kβ membrane recruitment. Both evaluations find strong support from TIRF microscopy data showing ~2000-fold binding frequency difference. Both emphasize that Gβγ and Rac1 alone have minimal recruitment capability.

Perfect agreement on claims C39-C44 regarding 1:1 binding stoichiometry. Both evaluations support the single-molecule diffusion analysis showing constant diffusion coefficients across varying pY densities. Peer review emphasizes the high quality and internal consistency of these results.

Perfect agreement on claims C26, C62 regarding novelty of membrane-conjugated approach. Both evaluations recognize this as a landmark technical advance over solution-based assays. Peer review emphasizes this enables observations impossible with bulk measurements and better mimics natural plasma membrane environment.

Strong agreement on claims C28-C29, C45-C49, C80-C81 regarding synergistic Gβγ binding and nSH2 competition mechanism. Both support the AlphaFold model and HDX-MS consistency. OpenEval notes caution about AlphaFold predictions; peer review similarly acknowledges 'no experimental structure to support this structural model' but finds it consistent with prior HDX-MS data.

Strong agreement on claims C50-C52 regarding Rac1(GTP) effects on PI3Kβ. Both evaluations support the modest enhancement of localization and ternary complex formation. Peer review treats Rac1 findings as part of comprehensive mechanistic characterization demonstrating unique activation by three inputs.

Strong agreement on claims C4-C5, C31-C32, C58, C60, C95 regarding allosteric activation exceeding recruitment effects. Both evaluations emphasize this as a central finding distinguishing recruitment from catalytic activation. Peer review identifies this as a key advance with all reviewers strongly supporting the two-phase ATP spike experimental design.

Agreement on claims C3, C53-C54, C61 regarding profound effects of membrane-conjugated peptides on enzyme activity. Both evaluations support the kinetic data. Peer review emphasizes the precision and clarity of mechanistic insight, while OpenEval provides more detailed analysis of kcat calculations and surface density measurements.

Agreement on claims C55-C56, C83 regarding Gβγ mutant controls and density requirements. Both evaluations support these as important mechanistic details. Peer review notes consistency with previous observations and validates the well-controlled experimental design.

Agreement on claim C59 regarding quantitative density-dependent measurements. Both evaluations support this as part of comprehensive kinetic characterization. Peer review emphasizes precision of mechanistic insight enabled by the reconstitution system.

Both address AlphaFold structural predictions (C77-C79). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to reliability concerns about protein-protein interface predictions, recommending experimental validation. Peer review is more accepting (SUPPORTED), acknowledging lack of experimental structure but finding model consistent with HDX-MS data and mutagenesis.

Partial overlap on claim C63 regarding cellular context speculation. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of direct experimental support in cells for PTEN-loss and EGFR density hypotheses. Peer review (R2) focuses on C3, C53-C54, C61 and does not specifically address the speculative cellular extrapolations in C63-C64, C100.

Agreement on claims C20-C21 as established background knowledge. Both evaluations recognize these as prior cellular observations providing context. Peer review notes current results clarify mechanistic basis of previous difficult-to-interpret cellular studies, reversing impression that all PI3Kβ inputs were equivalent.

Partial overlap on claims C89-C90 regarding background literature. Both evaluations support these as appropriate contextual citations. OpenEval groups extensive background claims (C67-C70, C82, C84-C92, C96-C99) as prior knowledge; peer review focuses on how current results clarify previous cellular observations.

Minimal overlap on claim C73 regarding PS-dependent enhancement. OpenEval (R7) specifically addresses C71-C75 on lipid composition effects as SUPPORTED. Peer review (R4) includes C73 among many claims about Gβγ mechanism but does not specifically discuss PS dependence.

Minimal overlap on claim C76. OpenEval groups C65-C66, C76, C88, C93 as SUPPORTED discussion points with appropriate citations. Peer review includes C76 in broader evaluation of Gβγ mechanism but does not specifically address the discussion interpretations.

Minimal overlap on claims C57, C94 regarding Rac1 kinetics. OpenEval includes these in comprehensive evaluation of Figure 5 kinetic data (C3-C5, C31-C32, C53-C54, C57-C58, C60-C61, C94-C95). Peer review addresses C50-C52, C57, C94 together, treating Rac1 as part of three-input activation mechanism.
